mechanics.name: Teamwork: Soft-Spoken
mechanics.currentEffect: For each other Survivor repairing a Generator with you, reduces the range at which its repair noises are heard by 15/20/25%. While repairing with at least one other Survivor, you repair 5% faster.
activation: Repair a Generator with at least one other Survivor for the 5% repair-speed bonus.
Each other Survivor repairing with you increases the noise-range reduction.
Ends/deactivates when: Bonuses end when you stop repairing with the other Survivor or Survivors.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.4.0): Introduced; no later material live balance change located in the official notes checked.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Cooperative repairs are faster and quieter for each teammate working on the Generator with you.
specialInteractions: The noise-range reduction scales for each other Survivor on the same Generator.

editorial.summary: While repairing with at least one teammate, repair 5% faster; each other Survivor also reduces the distance at which the generator's repair noise can be heard.
useCases: Add a modest repair bonus when the team deliberately stacks a generator.
Make cooperative generator work quieter on indoor or low-visibility maps.
Combine with other co-op perks during a planned burst repair.
counters: Five percent does not make inefficient generator stacking automatically good.
Quiet generator audio matters less when the Killer already knows the objective location.
cons: Lower ceiling than Prove Thyself or Friendly Competition.
Requires grouping Survivors on one objective.
analysis: Teamwork: Soft-Spoken lands at this position because five percent faster cooperative repair is useful, but Survivors do not need another excuse to over-stack generators. The bonus is best when two players already have a strategic reason to finish one objective immediately.

The quieter repair noise can help on indoor maps, especially when walls prevent the Killer from visually confirming the generator. With multiple teammates, the audible-distance reduction stacks through each additional Survivor.
The perk is easy to use and equally easy to overvalue. A five-percent modifier cannot repay every second lost by putting multiple Survivors on one generator instead of spreading map pressure.
That leaves Soft-Spoken as a modest co-op specialist. It has a clean floor when the trigger exists and no value at all when you are repairing alone.
editorial.verdict: A small co-op repair and stealth bonus that should follow good macro, not dictate it. Soft-Spoken is fine when stacking is already correct.
